basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma 'Natique sunt Heber filii duo: nomen uni Phaleg, eo quod in diebus ejus divisa sit terra,'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text: Natique sunt Heber filii duo: nomen uni Phaleg, eo quod in diebus ejus divisa sit terra, et nomen fratris ejus Jectan. Divisionem terrae eam dicit, quae in confusione linguarum facta est. Vocavit filium Phaleg, id est, Divisionem, ut perpetuam in hoc posteris suis memoriam suae devotionis relinqueret, quia nimirum, divisis ob superbiam linguis perfidorum, ipse merito fidei primitivam generis humani loquelam servaverit.
